query: For W–Cu metal-matrix composites used in heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications, what single intervention could increase thermal conductivity while retaining mechanical durability and irradiation resistance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an otherwise comparable W–Cu composite, defines the application conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of carbon nanotubes to W-Cu metal-matrix composites can increase thermal conductivity while retaining mechanical durability and irradiation resistance.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced phonon transport and thermal interface conductance
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased thermal conductivity relative to an otherwise comparable W-Cu composite
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 20-1000°C, neutron irradiation dose: 0-10 dpa
generation.uncertainty: Lack of data on long-term stability and irradiation resistance of carbon nanotube-reinforced W-Cu composites

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of thermal conductivity and mechanical properties between unmodified W-Cu composite and carbon nanotube-reinforced W-Cu composite after neutron irradiation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity of the carbon nanotube-reinforced W-Cu composite is not significantly higher than that of the unmodified W-Cu composite after neutron irradiation, or if the mechanical properties are compromised, the hypothesis is falsified.
